answer_markdown: For a **general aviation-single engine** aircraft, the typical horizontal tail volume coefficient ($C_{HT}$) is **0.70** and the vertical tail volume coefficient ($C_{VT}$) is **0.04** [1]. You can decrease these tail volume coefficients by **10-15%** if you use all-moving tail surfaces [3]. Additionally, a T-tail configuration allows a **5%** reduction in the vertical tail volume coefficient due to the end-plate effect [4], while T-tails and H-tails allow a **5%** reduction in the horizontal tail volume coefficient due to cleaner airflow [5].
